summary: Amazon cut about 16,000 corporate roles, a second large round after October 2025's 14,000. CEO Andy Jassy's memo said that as Amazon rolls out generative AI and agents it will need fewer people doing some current jobs; leadership also cited removing bureaucracy and management layers.
whyClassified: AI-driven efficiency was named alongside reducing bureaucracy, matching AI-related restructuring (C). It is a distinct 2026 round, not a restatement of the October 2025 cut.
whatWeKnow: Amazon confirmed about 16,000 corporate job cuts on January 28, 2026.
Jassy's memo tied generative AI and agents to needing fewer people in some roles.
whatWeDontKnow: How much of the 16,000 is attributable to AI versus removing management layers is not quantified.
Amazon did not disclose a US-versus-international split.
aiInvestmentContext: Amazon continues heavy AI infrastructure investment (Trainium, Bedrock, Anthropic stake).

locations.note: Global corporate reduction; no state-level breakdown published.

notes: Distinct round from amazon-2025-corporate-ai-efficiency; both are counted as separate announcements.

summary: Salesforce eliminated roughly 1,000 roles in early 2026 across marketing, product, data, and its Agentforce AI product, with further small rounds later in the year. CEO Marc Benioff has repeatedly credited AI automation for needing fewer people; Agentforce passed $1.2B in annual recurring revenue.
whyClassified: Benioff attributes the reductions directly to AI agents taking over work, matching direct AI replacement (A). It is a distinct 2026 round from the 2025 support reduction.
whatWeKnow: Salesforce confirmed about 1,000 roles cut in early 2026 across several teams.
A later June 2026 round documented 59 roles in Washington and 74 in California via WARN filings.
whatWeDontKnow: The full US-versus-international split of the early-2026 round was not disclosed.
How many affected staff moved to other internal roles is not specified.
aiInvestmentContext: Salesforce sells Agentforce and reports large productivity gains from AI coding agents.

locations.note: Global reduction; a later 2026 round documented small US numbers via WARN filings.

summary: Block laid off about 4,000 employees, roughly 40% of staff, reducing headcount from over 10,000 to under 6,000. Co-founder Jack Dorsey cited 'intelligence tools', and the CFO said the cuts would let the company move faster with smaller teams using AI to automate more work.
whyClassified: The company said AI automation enables far smaller teams, matching an AI-enabled productivity reduction (B).
whatWeKnow: Block confirmed about 4,000 cuts on February 26, 2026.
The CFO explicitly linked the reduction to using AI to automate work with smaller teams.
whatWeDontKnow: Block did not publish a US-versus-international or occupational breakdown.
How much of the reduction reflects prior over-hiring versus AI specifically is not quantified.
aiInvestmentContext: Block has emphasised AI tooling across Square and Cash App.

locations.note: Company-wide reduction; no state-level breakdown published.

summary: Snap cut about 1,000 roles, 16% of its workforce. A company memo said rapid advances in AI let its teams reduce repetitive work and increase velocity; CEO Evan Spiegel said small squads were already using AI tools heavily. Snap projected over $500 million in annual expense savings.
whyClassified: Snap stated AI lets it operate with fewer people doing repetitive work, matching an AI-enabled productivity reduction (B).
whatWeKnow: Snap confirmed about 1,000 cuts (16%) in April 2026 and removed 300+ open roles.
The memo credited AI with reducing repetitive work.
whatWeDontKnow: Snap did not disclose a US-versus-international breakdown.
The split between AI-driven and cost-driven reductions is not quantified.
aiInvestmentContext: Snap has invested in AI features across Snapchat and its advertising tools.

summary: PayPal said it would cut about 4,760 roles (20% of staff) phased over two to three years, as new CEO Enrique Lores stripped out redundant structures and accelerated AI integration. PayPal created an 'AI transformation and simplification' team and targeted at least $1.5 billion in savings from the cuts and AI-enabled processes.
whyClassified: PayPal tied the reduction to simplification and reallocating toward AI-native operations, matching AI capital reallocation (D). Because it is a multi-year phased plan, it is recorded as planned.
whatWeKnow: PayPal announced about 4,760 cuts (20%) phased over two to three years.
The plan pairs the reduction with an AI-transformation program targeting $1.5B in savings.
whatWeDontKnow: As a multi-year plan, how many roles have actually been eliminated so far is not established.
PayPal did not attribute specific eliminated roles to AI performing the work.
aiInvestmentContext: PayPal appointed a Chief AI Transformation & Simplification Officer to lead its AI agenda.

whyClassified: Prince explicitly attributed the reduction to AI changing the work and stated it was not driven by weak business, matching an AI-enabled productivity reduction (B).
whatWeKnow: Cloudflare confirmed about 1,100 cuts (20%) on May 7, 2026, alongside record revenue.

whatWeDontKnow: Cloudflare did not publish a US-versus-international breakdown.

whatWeDontKnow: How much of the 8,000 reflects performance-based exits versus AI reallocation is not cleanly separable.

summary: Oracle ended fiscal 2026 with about 141,000 employees, roughly 21,000 fewer than a year earlier. Its SEC filing stated that the adoption and deployment of AI technologies across operations 'have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce', listing AI among several factors including management and product changes, performance, strategic shifts, and acquisitions.
whyClassified: A binding SEC filing names AI among multiple restructuring factors, matching AI-related restructuring (C). It is one of the strongest AI-attribution sources in the dataset, but the AI-specific share is not quantified.
whatWeKnow: Oracle's headcount fell about 21,000 year-over-year (roughly 13%).
Its SEC filing explicitly links AI adoption to workforce reductions.
whatWeDontKnow: The 21,000 is a net year-over-year headcount decline that also reflects attrition, acquisitions, performance, and strategic changes; the AI-specific portion is not quantified.
Oracle did not publish a US-versus-international breakdown, and teams on AI/cloud infrastructure were largely spared.
aiInvestmentContext: Oracle is expanding Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and AI data centers; some AI teams grew even as overall headcount fell.

locations.note: Global reduction; no state-level breakdown published.

notes: Headcount is a net year-over-year decline; the AI-specific share is unquantified. Recorded at MEDIUM confidence despite the SEC source because AI is one of several stated factors.

whyClassified: Microsoft explicitly said the cuts are not AI replacing employees, only that AI is reshaping the sector. With no company causal claim, this is context only (F) and is excluded from all AI-attributed totals.
whatWeKnow: Microsoft confirmed about 4,800 cuts on July 6, 2026.
The company acknowledged AI is reshaping work but denied AI directly replaced these roles.
whatWeDontKnow: Microsoft did not attribute the cuts to AI causally, so no AI-attributed headcount is counted.
Whether AI investment influenced the decision is not established.
aiInvestmentContext: Microsoft continues very large AI infrastructure investment and is a major OpenAI backer.
